By outlining how each device works and what they protect against, clearly explain why it is necessary to have both of these devices installed in order for residents to be fully protected.

In order to protect against household fires and electrocution, modern buildings are equipped with RCD’s and Circuit Breakers. By outlining how each device works and what they protect against, clearly explain why it is necessary to have both of these devices installed in order for residents to be fully protected.

Circuit breakers are designed to break the circuit when particularly high currents are detected 1 mark
Circuit breakers protect against household fires because high currents can result in overheating of wires, which can cause household fires 1 mark
When someone is being electrocuted, however, it is not expected that the current through the circuit breaker would be high, so the circuit will not be broken. 1 mark
An RCD is designed to break the circuit when it detects a difference between the currents in the active and neutral wires 1 mark
RCDs protect against electrocution as current flowing through a person and out of the circuit will result in a difference in current between the active and neutral wires 1 mark
RCDs won’t protect against household fires, however, as they are not sensitive to the size of the current in either wire, only the difference in current between them. 1 mark
